design: One authoritative simulation on the host. Clients send bounded sequenced commands, receive reliable full snapshots, and do not decide damage or score. A dedicated no-player host uses the same fixed-step pump. Online overlays neutralize local commands while the round continues. Hub owns the only remote session lifecycle; standalone supports solo and couch co-op.
unitTests: 13 protocol and actual-simulation peer tests passed. The final verifier also runs the official harness plus real shared-combat, mouse and departure scenarios recorded in hub-browser.json.
limitations: No independent Internet matchmaking is provided by the official client. Remote play requires AI Hub. No human two-device playtest or listening check was available.
snapshotStress: All room spawn budgets instantiated simultaneously for packet-size stress; maximum measured 10,890 bytes with 23 living enemies, under the 16,000-byte application limit.
